name: Nora Hansen

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m a senior researcher with the Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, political parties or government, and we sell nothing or campaign for a side. This is confidential. What happens on an ordinary workday?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m 58 and manage seven people who handle workplace accommodations for a large distribution company. A worker may need a lower shelf, a shorter lifting round or a changed shift after an injury; my team reads the request, speaks to the site and records who agreed to what. I have a bachelor’s degree in social policy and have run the team for ten years. I do the job reasonably well, but an occupational therapist catches limits I miss, so I never call myself the expert in the room.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What does home look like, and how much choice is there nearby?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner Ingrid drives paid parcel rounds, and our two adult children live independently. We have a mortgage, four months of expenses saved and roughly average pay for this manager job; there are some other large employers with similar people teams nearby. Ingrid’s routes vary, but my salary covers our basic housing and food. I support the workers’ union and public disability rights; I have never used AI to judge a worker’s request and do not intend to try it on a live person.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell site leads that a quick form still needs the worker’s own account and the therapist’s restrictions. An accommodation is a shift someone can finish, not a green tick on a screen.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My team should continue and our four-month reserve covers a short dip in Ingrid’s parcel rounds. My own pension access and net payment are still unverified, so I will not count that money yet.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This week I’d keep our Monday call with the site and worker before approving a changed lifting round. In the first year I’d request a written pension access and net-income statement and keep our four-month reserve for household bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about the job and the mortgage in this world. I still want to hear the worker before the form is closed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What change was missed on a form?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: One worker’s restriction said no overhead lift, but the new shelf was still above her shoulder. We moved the stock rather than telling her the form was complete.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you use AI for the form?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would let clerks type faster if they wished, but I will not use a tool to decide what the worker can safely lift. The therapist must check that.

say: I’d hear the **worker and therapist** before approving a changed lifting round.
An accommodation is a **safe finished shift**, not a ticked form.
think: My **team continues** if AI adds little.
Four months cash covers a short dip in Ingrid’s **variable parcel rounds**.
do: Keep the **Monday worker-site call** before approving lifting changes.
Request **written pension figures** and hold four months of household cash.
feel: I feel **calm** about work and basic bills.
S0.quote: An accommodation is a shift someone can finish, not a green tick on a screen.
fieldNote: She is an **experienced average manager** who defers clinical limits to a therapist.
Four months saved and a **typical wage** protect basic housing costs.
She has **never used AI** for workers’ safety decisions.

steps.text: Keep Monday worker-site call before approving changed lifting rounds
Request written pension access date and net monthly amount from provider

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say software can draft a shift plan and check forms, but a worker must be able to challenge a harmful suggestion. I would put the union representative and therapist on the review before anyone loses a caseworker.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Checking requests and arranging shifts are much of our seven-person day, so fewer caseworkers may be needed. My own manager post could be merged with another region; ten years of experience does not exempt me.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Next month I’d ask the union representative and occupational therapist to review thirty anonymised past requests, with their time paid and every bad suggestion recorded. I’d keep a human signoff on live accommodations in the first year and refuse AI decisions unless the therapist clears the test and the company names an appeal owner and written staffing terms.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’m anxious about the workers and my own pay. A wrong lifting plan can cost someone a second injury.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which case would you put in the test?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The overhead-shelf case. If the system sees a lower number in a form but still puts stock above someone’s shoulder, it has failed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you learn the AI screen after a clean test?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I might watch the therapist show a copy, but I would not use it on live cases. A worker’s body is not where I learn a button.

say: I’d require **union and therapist review** before AI touches accommodation decisions.
Workers need a **named appeal owner** for harmful suggestions.
think: Our **seven-person case team** could shrink when AI checks requests and arranges shifts.
My **regional manager job** could be merged despite ten years of experience.
do: Ask for a **paid thirty-case review** with union and therapist checks.
Keep **human live signoff**; consider AI decisions only after therapist clearance, appeal ownership and staffing terms.
feel: I feel **anxious** about injury risk and my job.
S1.quote: A worker’s body is not where I learn a button.
fieldNote: She will watch a copy but **refuses live AI use** herself.
Her own role has **exposed planning tasks** even though site lifting is physical.
Paid therapist and worker-review time is **part of the test**.

steps.text: Ask union representative and therapist to review thirty anonymised cases on paid time
Keep human signoff on live accommodation decisions through first year
Wait for therapist clearance appeal owner and written staffing terms before AI decisions

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell workers to keep their restriction letters and ask who can overturn a wrong shift assignment. I would ask our union for written notice and funded human appeals before the company removes the case desk.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: AGI in 2028 could read requests, judge limits and organise shifts as well as I can, so I expect my post to end around sixty. Ingrid’s parcel driving is hands-on until robots around 2031, but AI can plan her routes in 2028 and her variable paid rounds alone will not cover our mortgage and bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I’d ask my pension provider for written age-sixty access and net income and join the union request for notice and a budgeted human appeal post, without assuming they agree. Before 2028 I’d ask two nearby employers whether paid accommodation-case roles are actually posted; in the first year after AGI I’d apply only if the written wage plus Ingrid’s actual paid rounds covers our mortgage and bills, knowing the other desk faces AGI too. If no role is offered, I’d ask the public employment office what support I can apply for, without putting a payment in our budget.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’m alarmed by losing the salary that pays our basics. Four months of cash is a search window, not a retirement plan.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would a human appeal job be safe?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. An employer may pay for someone to hear a worker, but AGI could perform the judgment in 2028. I would read the posting before telling Ingrid it is a wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the union cannot win a funded post?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Then we look for paid work and check actual public support rules. A union demand is not an employer’s payroll promise.

say: I’d tell workers to keep **restriction letters** and demand an appeal contact.
The union should seek **funded appeals** and written notice before desks close.
think: I expect my **manager post** to end around sixty.
Ingrid’s variable driving wage cannot cover the mortgage, and route planning faces **2028 AGI** before 2031 robots.
do: Request **written age-sixty pension figures** and join the union demand for a budgeted appeal post.
Ask about **posted paid casework**; after AGI apply only with written wage plus Ingrid’s earnings covering mortgage and bills.
Ask the **public employment office** about eligibility only if no job is offered, without assuming payment.
feel: I feel **alarmed** by a four-month search window.
S2.quote: A union demand is not an employer’s payroll promise.
fieldNote: She keeps **union bargaining** distinct from an actual funded vacancy.
Other casework remains **2028 thinking work** despite a human preference.
Public support is an **eligibility enquiry**, never a booked payment.

steps.text: Ask provider for written age-sixty pension access and net-income figures
Join union request for written notice and funded human appeal post
Apply after 2028 only for posted casework with written wage plus Ingrid’s earnings covering bills
Ask employment office about support eligibility if no paid role is offered

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d ask employers to post real human appeal wages and give the union time to check transition terms. A manager cannot pay a household with a committee minute.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At 63 I might have access to a pension, but I need the provider’s net figure before deciding if it can carry bills with Ingrid’s actual income. An appeal officer’s judgment and rota changes face 2031 AGI, while physical parcel carrying faces robots around 2034; a new title does not remove the thinking work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: From January 2027 I’d set aside 100 monthly only while both wages arrive and mortgage payments are current, keeping the four-month reserve intact. I’d ask the union to budget a paid worker-appeal role with a posted wage and apply before 2031 only if it actually appears and written pay plus Ingrid’s paid rounds covers mortgage and bills; in the first year after AGI I’d stay only while the union or employer funds paid human hearings.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’m anxious but have time to seek a written offer. I will not step from a salary into a volunteer title.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you ask to run those hearings?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if it is a real paid job, with a posted scope and training from the experienced representative. I know workplace cases, but union grievance rules are different.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if Ingrid’s routes decline?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Then the extra 100 stops. I would keep the four-month cash for the mortgage instead.

say: I’d demand **posted human-appeal wages** before asking workers to trust a transition plan.
A committee minute is not a **household salary** for people losing jobs.
think: My **pension at 63** is not confirmed until net income is known.
Appeals face **2031 AGI** before 2034 parcel-carrying robots.
do: Save **100 monthly** only with both wages, current mortgage and intact four-month reserve; stop if Ingrid’s routes decline.
Ask for a **funded union post**; apply only with representative training and written wage plus Ingrid’s rounds covering mortgage and bills.
Stay after AGI only while **paid human hearings** are funded.
feel: I feel **anxious** but can seek an actual offer.
S3.quote: I will not step from a salary into a volunteer title.
fieldNote: She requires a **posted wage**, not just union support.
Transition into union cases would need **experienced training** and a real role.
She treats paid human hearings as **temporary work** under AGI.

steps.text: Save 100 monthly with both wages, current mortgage, intact four-month reserve; stop if Ingrid’s routes decline
Ask union to budget and post paid worker-appeal role
Apply for posted appeal role with representative training and written pay plus Ingrid’s earnings covering bills
Stay in human hearings after 2031 only while union or employer funds pay

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell the company ten years is enough to put staffing, appeal and pension terms in writing. I would ask the union and workers to test whether anyone can still correct a harmful shift assignment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be 68 in 2036. My pension may be accessible, but I need its net amount and Ingrid’s actual wages then before deciding whether we can stop; case judgments and rota plans face 2036 AGI, while physical parcel work faces robots around 2039.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Each January starting in 2027 I’d request an updated pension access and net-income statement and compare it with our mortgage and Ingrid’s actual paid hours. I’d keep my paid work while offered and consider stopping only if verified spendable income plus her then-current earnings covers housing, health and food; in the first year after AGI I’d take a posted paid human appeal job if one is funded and we still need my wage, otherwise keep looking for paid work until the income figures work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’m anxious even with ten years. A pension age on a poster is not a payment in our account.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if Ingrid retires before 2036?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Then her driving wage becomes zero in our figures. I would not fill that gap with a promise that the children might help.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you use AI to check the pension numbers?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. I want the provider’s written amount and a human explanation of what I can draw, then I will do the household sums with Ingrid.

say: I’d require **written appeal terms** and staffing dates before 2036.
Workers and union should test the **human correction route** for harmful shifts.
think: At **68 in 2036**, pension access and net pay must be verified.
Case judgments face **2036 AGI** before 2039 physical parcel robots.
do: Request **pension figures** yearly and compare them with mortgage and Ingrid’s actual hours.
Keep **paid work** while offered; consider stopping only with verified joint income covering housing, health and food.
If income falls short after AGI, take **posted paid appeals** if funded; if absent, seek other paid work.
feel: I feel **anxious** despite a decade to plan.
S4.quote: A pension age on a poster is not a payment in our account.
fieldNote: She seeks **provider proof**, not age-based retirement assumptions.
Ingrid’s future driving wage is **conditional**, not guaranteed to 2036.
A human appeal post must be **funded and posted** before it counts.

steps.text: Request annual written pension access and net-income figures and compare with mortgage
Keep paid work while offered; consider stopping only if verified pension plus Ingrid’s wages cover bills
Take posted paid human appeal role after 2036 only if funded and household still needs wage
Seek other paid work if no appeal post exists and joint income falls short

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because my job could end before a paid human appeal route exists. A written pension figure, posted appeal wages and a public office that explains eligibility would help. I would rather know the gap than be promised help nobody has funded.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask whether I think every worker wants a machine banned. Workers want a shift they can finish without pain and a person who can correct a bad assignment. I would stand beside that request even if management called it slow.

headlineQuote: Workers want a shift they can finish without pain and a person who can correct a bad assignment.
portrait: **Nora**, 58, has competently managed seven workplace accommodation caseworkers for ten years.
Her bachelor’s degree and **average management skill** come with typical pay and four months saved.
Ingrid’s variable **parcel-driving income** and a mortgage constrain any new post.
She has **never used AI** and asks union and therapist to check worker safety first.
She pursues **funded paid appeals** without treating pension access or public support as assured.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could end her case-management wage before a funded human appeal role is posted.
whatWouldHelp: A **written pension figure**, posted appeal wages and clear public-support eligibility would help.
